title: A connected characteristic-zero group with semisimple Lie algebra is semisimple
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field]. Let $H$ be a geometrically connected affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Geometrically connected means connected after algebraic closure [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Equip its identity tangent space $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space, def-sc-dual-numbers] with the bracket induced by group commutators. If this finite-dimensional Lie algebra is semisimple [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], then $H$ is semisimple: after extension to an algebraic closure it has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme. A closed subgroup is [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and solvable means that its successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups eventually become trivial. No splitness or simply-connectedness hypothesis is imposed, and the trivial group is allowed.

source.place: Lemma 23.68, printed p.506, implication from semisimple Lie algebra to semisimple connected algebraic group. This is the converse direction to the existing lem-sfb-char-zero-semisimple-group-lie.

proof.text: Let $i:N\hookrightarrow H$ be any smooth connected commutative affine $k$-group scheme of finite type with a closed normal subgroup inclusion, as in the test of [lem-sfb-perfect-field-semisimple-commutative-test]. By [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-lie-ideal], $di$ is injective and its image $I\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ is an ideal with $[I,I]=0$.

The first derived term of $I$ is $[I,I]=0$, so $I$ is solvable by [def-wf-lie-algebra]. The hypothesis that $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ is semisimple, in [def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], therefore gives $I=0$. Injectivity of $di$ now gives $\operatorname{Lie}(N)=0$.

source.place: Lemma 23.68 (p.506): the commutative Lie ideal vanishes.

proof.text: The identity subgroup $e_H\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$ is closed in $H$: if $H=\operatorname{Spec}B$, its identity is cut out by the kernel of the surjective augmentation $B\to k$. Its tangent space is zero, since its only dual-number point over its identity is the identity itself [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-charzero-lie-detects-factorization] to $f=i:N\to H$ and $K=e_H$: its source is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, the field has characteristic zero, and $di(\operatorname{Lie}(N))=0\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(e_H)$. Thus $i$ factors through $e_H$. Let $u:N\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be this factorization and $v:\operatorname{Spec}k\to N$ its identity section. Then $i\circ v\circ u=i$; as $i$ is a subgroup inclusion, $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$. Also $u\circ v=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$. Hence $N$ is the trivial group scheme.

source.place: Lemma 23.68 (p.506), zero Lie algebra forces finiteness; the sharper connected conclusion is obtained directly from 10.14--10.15 (pp.190--191), in the existing factorization form.

proof.text: A characteristic-zero field is perfect: an irreducible polynomial of positive degree has nonzero derivative of smaller degree, so is coprime to its derivative and has no repeated root. Since the subgroup $N$ above was arbitrary, condition (2) of [lem-sfb-perfect-field-semisimple-commutative-test] holds. Apply that criterion to the given smooth geometrically connected affine finite-type group $H$. It gives precisely the required absence of nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroups after algebraic closure. The argument also applies to the trivial group.

source.place: Proposition 19.3 (p.398), used in the forward implication of Lemma 23.68 (p.506); Proposition 19.1 (p.397) accounts for the geometric meaning.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 23.68, printed p.506, semisimple-Lie-algebra implication, expanded using Proposition 19.3 (p.398) and the existing tangent-factorization corollary of 10.14--10.15 (pp.190--191).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q77-225c32d32 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and Milne iAG2017 at the cited places: Lemma 23.68 (p.506), Prop 19.1–19.3 and 6.44 (pp.397–398), and 10.14, 10.23, 10.28–10.31. The item statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1 uses normal-subgroup-lie-ideal: the tangent map is injective and its image is an ideal I with zero bracket; this is true in every characteristic by the stabiliser argument of Milne 10.31. Step 2 is elementary: I is solvable, so semisimplicity of Lie(H) gives Lie(N)=0. Step 3 applies lie-detects-factorization with K=e_H. Its hypotheses hold (char 0, N smooth connected affine of finite type, e_H closed, Lie(e_H)=0). The inverse morphisms u,v and cancellation by the monomorphism i are written out, so N is trivial. Step 4 notes that a characteristic-zero field is perfect and applies condition (2)⇒(1) of the new test node. Its conclusion is exactly the item's conclusion. New node perfect-field-semisimple-commutative-test is Milne 19.3 with semisimple unfolded via 6.44 and perfectness defined inline and kept. I tested it on SL_2 with mu_2 (not connected, so excluded), on G_a, G_m, B_2 and GL_2 (each fails condition (2)), and on the imperfect-field case, where the converse is not claimed. New node normal-subgroup-lie-ideal I tested on mu_p in G_m, alpha_p, and the unipotent subgroup of B_2 (no centrality is claimed). Neither node restates a clause of the item, both are statement-only, and the B1–B5 form checks pass. Duplicate search: rg over the snapshot DAG; reductive-radical-quotient, char-zero-semisimple-group-lie, affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus and lie-normalizer-centralizer-invariants all differ. No cycle: the only citer is split-charzero-lie-group-integration. Batch-5 flag: lie-detects-factorization reaches lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion through the group-smoothness chain. That node is the general criterion for smoothness at a point of a flat morphism, not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality statements or proofs, so the citation is accepted. No changes and no tool_uses.
